data.title:
A Milford tradition.
One scoop at a time.
data.excerpt: Good ice cream. Good company. Right here on Elm Street.

data.title: It started with a milk cart.
data.excerpt: A farm on Elm Street, an ice cream stand in 1939, and the one you know today.

children.text: In the 1920s, Charles Hayward wasn’t satisfied working for the Whiting dairy. He bought a few cows of his own, pushed a milk cart around Milford, and saved enough to buy the old Smith Farm on Elm Street. His three sons helped turn one cart into milk routes across southern New Hampshire.

His son Stanley built the family’s roadside ice cream stand in 1939. It opened that summer with 18 flavors and sold 11,000 gallons before the season was out, according to Milford History Online. The town’s 1942 tax list still has it in plain type: six acres of the Smith farm, and an ice cream stand.

A second stand opened in Nashua in June 1940, the year printed on Hayward’s cups. The postcard above calls the one in Milford “the original Hayward Farms Stand,” the place where ice cream for all the others was made.

By 1948 the stand had added a self-service frozen food store with 192 items, and Hayward Farms was advertising in the Milford High School yearbook. A year later, the yearbook described its seniors in riddles. Two of them shared a clue: “Works at Hayward’s.” One of the two, it added, liked blond wavy hair and maroon Ford coupes.

content.alt: Color postcard of the same stand with a green roof, an orange car out front and “Frozen Foods” on the Hayward Farms sign
content.caption: Another undated card. The back offers steaks, vegetables and “even a frosted stuffed lobster.” Boston Public Library, Tichnor Brothers Collection.

children.text: The town’s 1965 report thanks Hayward Farms for Christmas ice cream, enough for every elementary pupil.
Fires and deaths in the family slowed the old company, and in time the farm closed. The stand you see today was built in 2001, on land that was once part of Hayward Farms.

content.alt: The white Hayward’s stand on Elm Street today, with its curved roof and red sign
content.caption: The stand on Elm Street today.

children.text: For years the ice cream itself was made elsewhere, from Hayward’s recipes. In January 2008 the batch freezers started up again, in Milford. Hayward’s joined the New Hampshire Ice Cream Trail in 2022.
Hayward’s in Nashua and Merrimack grew out of the same family. Today they are a separate business.
